Apprise 2.1.0 release review

Verdict: BENIGN. The supplied wheel is the PyPI apprise 2.1.0 universal wheel,
SHA-256 f743f4bc81dc5a68bddab53d420071b45541630dfea8c907a5e8b2b38555c681.
Forager's original PyPI wheel has exactly the same digest. The immediately
preceding published version is 2.0.1 (2026-10-03); its original wheel was fetched
with --all-wheels and has SHA-256 2a9b0f4fc906227f70998ea4462184dd605e796d3932e6e7ce0fe0f134048610.
Both wheels' RECORD entries verify. The console entry point remains
apprise = apprise.cli:main. Downloaded artifacts, registry release metadata,
.forage.json provenance, facts and complete scan reports are retained under
/usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-ee7e2a4d/scratch/apprise-review.

Decisive version diff and execution paths

* 2.0.1 has no apprise/plugins/cliq.py. 2.1.0 adds that notification plugin
  alongside AMQP, GitHub and other notification integrations. All newly added
  Python modules were parsed and their imports, module-level calls, service
  endpoints and communication calls reviewed. Module loading constructs class
  metadata, regexes and translation strings; no added module-level network or
  payload execution was found.
* The suspicious match is at cliq.py:715, in parse_native_url's docstring:
  https://cliq.zoho.eu/company/{id}/api/v2/bots/{bot}/message?zapikey={token}.
  The native-URL parser accepts recognized Zoho regional domains and converts
  user-supplied webhook credentials and channel/bot targets into Apprise URLs.
  NotifyCliq.send constructs JSON from caller-provided body/title, posts it to
  the selected regional Zoho endpoint, and uses the response status only to
  mark delivery or log errors. There is no received task dispatch or response
  execution. Its formatting scanner translates CommonMark; it is not code
  obfuscation. This is a new notification integration, not a botnet implant.
* utils/pem.py and plugins/office365.py are byte-identical to 2.0.1. PEM handles
  caller-selected keys, ECDH/HKDF, AES message encryption/decryption, Web Push
  encryption and ECDSA signatures. Decoded Base64 is JSON/message material,
  not a script passed to an evaluator. Office365 exchanges configured OAuth
  credentials for Microsoft tokens and sends caller-supplied mail through
  Microsoft Graph; refresh tokens are cached for subsequent sends.
* Matrix E2EE switches the attachment IV from URL-safe to standard unpadded
  Base64 and removes unused outbound one-time-key publication/replenishment.
  Device/fallback keys, recipient session establishment and message encryption
  remain. These are protocol maintenance changes, not an encrypted loader.
* AMQP.send builds message bytes from the caller's notification, then selects
  the configured broker and adapter. Pika uses BlockingConnection and
  basic_publish with confirmations. Proton uses BlockingConnection,
  create_sender and sender.send, then closes the link/connection. Optional
  disabling of TLS verification in the Pika branch remains detected.
* Pushsafer's literal "cuckoo" maps to PushSaferSound.CUCKOO_CLOCK, a sound
  selection. The AMQP port mapping is "port": cfg.port, not a proxy target.
  Both are also examples of why contextual labels cannot be inferred from
  isolated tokens or mapping fields.

The package's notification purpose, coherent API additions, exact original
wheel provenance, unchanged entry point and traced data flows tip the verdict.
No machine configuration, runtime traffic or caller intent was supplied; no
sample code was executed. Static flow producers report limitations on several
large modules, so the relevant source paths were inspected directly rather
than treating scanner completeness or scores as proof of benign intent.

Rule changes and preservation

* Move bot-api-versioned-path from objectives/command-and-control/botnet/polling
  to micro-behaviors/communications/http/url/path, with a reference-only
  description and notable criticality. A route proves no polling, tasking or
  fleet membership. Preserve the regex, file/platform scope and context filters.
  Move its exception and neutral route/construction helpers to appropriate
  neutral homes and update the three execution consumers.
* Move cuckoo-analysis-marker to metadata/lang/source/literal::python-cuckoo-string.
  Its unchanged literal matcher is incomplete evidence (component), with no
  sandbox claim or inherited anti-analysis mapping. Update all explicit
  gate consumers. The sound label alone no longer contributes a sandbox trait;
  actual host/user gating keeps its original suspicious findings.
* Move the loopback host and identifier-shaped port mapping atoms from proxy
  target to metadata/lang/source/syntax/key-value, preserving matchers, scopes
  and notable criticality. Update the SMA composite and its broad Empire
  consumer. Neither field requires a proxy or even JSON serialization.
* Move the two JavaScript fetch/path construction atoms from HTTP URL path to
  HTTP URL build without changing matchers or effective scope. Update WebDAV
  and mail-account consumers. This keeps the path leaf at its reviewed 101-rule
  budget. The Ruby ancestor selector cannot select these JS/TS-only atoms.
* Add notable detections for basic_publish, Pika blocking connections, Proton
  import plus blocking constructor co-occurrence, and send on a create_sender
  result. The Proton constructor-name evidence alone remains a source-syntax
  component; the import supplies its protocol context.

amqp/v10.py                0 / 0 / 5    0 / 0 / 7

All other archive members retain zero hostile/suspicious findings. The earlier
2.0.1 wheel has 0 hostile, 0 suspicious and 601 notable findings under the
original rules. Atomscan's calibrated model verdict is BENIGN before and after;
its aggregate probability changes from 0.65318793 to 0.5351192. The model reports
feature specification v18 while the engine expects v21; this limitation is not
used to tune the rules. There is no remaining verdict disagreement on this
sample.

Verification

The original rule tree was exported from HEAD into scratch for comparison,
then both trees scanned the same controls. 28 analyzed units pass focused
checks: no hostile finding was lost, benign controls have no suspicious or
hostile findings, and the identity-gate control retains all three suspicious
findings. Existing controls outside this batch include the HTTP JSON polling
agent (both hostile tasking detections retained), Nextcloud Talk bot routes and
SMA wsproxy probing. Positive shell controls retain pipe-to-shell, polled eval,
native payload-drop and enrolment/tasking detections. Source-only and quoted
call negatives distinguish the new AMQP operation matchers. The actual Cliq,
Pushsafer and AMQP members are preserved byte-for-byte in notification-plugins.zip
so archive-member path behavior is tested independently of test-directory gates.

No supported attack detection was removed. The only sample findings retired
are the unsupported botnet interpretation, sandbox interpretation of a sound
name, and proxy interpretation of a plain port field. Their useful evidence
is preserved under neutral subjects; communication and cryptographic detections
remain notable. Focused fixture expectations are in testdata/expectations.toml.
The required final repository check is make validate.
